# Results — Study 457 (Kicker-Pattern)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **the
kicker (two opposite marubozu candles separated by a gap in the new direction) marks a violent,
reliable turn; trade its direction** — encoded as a mechanical rule. A marubozu is a strong
candle (body / range ≥ 0.60); a kicker at bar `t` is an opposite-colour marubozu pair where
bar `t` gaps in its own direction past bar `t-1`'s open. We go long a bullish kicker / short a
bearish one, entered at the **next close** (one documented lag), and measure the forward
5/10/20/60-day return (signed by the kicker direction). Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **80** mechanical kickers pooled across the 5 tapes (**43 bullish / 37 bearish**, marubozu body-frac = 0.60) |
| Timing / costs | pattern read on the close of bar *t* (uses only *t-1*, *t*); enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per kicker |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. Note that adjustment shrinks raw gaps; the rare, strict marubozu+gap
> kicker is therefore a low-frequency event (80 in 21 years across 5 tapes), which is itself a
> finding: the canonical pattern almost never prints on liquid index ETFs. The Signal axis uses
> a **direction-matched random-entry** baseline (same long/short mix, same instrument, same
> epoch, same hold), so the upward drift every long inherits is neutralized.

## The signal — kicker direction vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* against zero is meaningless for a mixed long/short rule on a drifting tape; the
**Welch kicker-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = kicker − random.

| horizon | n | kicker | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (kicker−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 80 | −7.1 bps  | 49% | −0.20 | +30.6 bps | **−37.7 bps** | −9.1 bps  | −0.96 | 0.339 |
| 10-day | 80 | −17.8 bps | 46% | −0.43 | +37.4 bps | **−55.2 bps** | −19.8 bps | −1.13 | 0.260 |
| 20-day | 80 | −19.1 bps | 51% | −0.35 | +34.5 bps | **−53.5 bps** | −21.1 bps | −0.78 | 0.438 |
| 60-day | 78 | +13.6 bps | 54% | +0.11 | +34.5 bps | **−20.9 bps** | +11.6 bps | −0.15 | 0.878 |

Read it carefully. The kicker direction **loses to a drift-matched random entry at every
horizon** (Δ = −37.7 / −55.2 / −53.5 / −20.9 bps), and the kicker-vs-random Welch *t* is
**negative everywhere** — it never comes close to the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar (best is −0.15 at 60
days). The "violent reliable turn" is not even a coin flip: at 5–20 days you'd do *better*
entering on random days. The kicker does not forecast.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — no coherent edge anywhere

| ticker | entries | kicker | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (kicker−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 13 | +121.7 bps | +0.82 | +45.9 bps | **+75.8 bps** |
| QQQ | 16 | +147.5 bps | +1.03 | +77.9 bps | **+69.5 bps** |
| IWM | 5  | −385.2 bps | n/a    | +20.6 bps | **−405.9 bps** |
| DIA | 12 | −76.0 bps  | −0.44  | −2.1 bps  | **−73.9 bps** |
| GLD | 34 | −77.3 bps  | −1.38  | +30.0 bps | **−107.3 bps** |

SPY and QQQ show a *nominally* positive delta but neither one-sample *t* clears 1.1, on 13–16
trades — noise. IWM has 5 trades (uninterpretable). DIA and GLD are negative. There is **no
coherent cross-sectional edge** — the hallmark of a pattern that isn't doing anything.

## Gap-scramble geometry placebo — the structure isn't load-bearing (and is incoherent where it's "positive")

The decisive "does the gap-reversal geometry matter?" test: keep every bar's marubozu colour
(the candle marginal), but permute the day-over-day open-gap signs, so the "gap in the new
direction" becomes random. If the kicker's gap really carried information, the scramble would
collapse the result.

| ticker | observed kicker 20d | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | +121.7 bps | 0.002 | 500 |
| QQQ | +147.5 bps | 0.002 | 500 |
| IWM | −385.2 bps | 1.000 | 500 |
| DIA | −76.0 bps  | 0.996 | 500 |
| GLD | −77.3 bps  | 0.976 | 500 |

This is **not** evidence the geometry forecasts. The two low-*p* tickers (SPY, QQQ) are exactly
the ones whose tiny kicker sample (13, 16 trades) happens to be positive — and they *still fail*
the drift-matched random test above (Welch deltas are noise). The scramble can't beat a positive
small-sample mean simply because permuting the gap signs usually changes which few bars qualify.
On the other three tapes the geometry is *useless or harmful* (*p* ≥ 0.976). A signal that
forecasts has a **coherent** placebo across instruments; this one doesn't. The gap-reversal
geometry is not load-bearing.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real continuation

On a deterministic tape that plants genuine kicker formations and then pushes the following days
in the kicker's direction (knob `edge`), the same rule behaves exactly as it must — so the flat
real-tape result is a genuine "nothing there", not a dead detector. (seed 458, n_days = 6000.)

| planted edge | n | kicker | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (formation, no continuation) | 156 | +0.6 bps   | 49% | +0.02 |
| **0.60** (real planted continuation)  | 156 | +547.4 bps | 79% | **+10.35** |

With the formation present but **no** planted continuation the control sits at *t* ≈ 0 (win 49%
— no false positive); a real planted continuation lights up at *t* = +10.35 with a 79% win-rate.
The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The kicker direction **loses to a drift-matched random baseline at every
  horizon** (kicker − random = −37.7 / −55.2 / −53.5 / −20.9 bps at 5/10/20/60 days; the Welch
  *t* is negative everywhere, best −0.15). Even the one-sample mean is roughly zero (−7 to −19
  bps at 5–20 days). There is no edge to find.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Nothing to deploy: the rule fires ~4×/year per tape and underperforms
  random entries; costs (1 bp × 2 legs) deepen the hole. A 50/50 win-rate with a negative mean is
  the opposite of "one of the most reliable signals."
- **"Does the gap-reversal forecast?" — BUSTED.** The gap-scramble placebo is incoherent — the
  only two low-*p* tickers (SPY, QQQ) are noisy small-sample positives that *fail* the random
  test, while the other three give *p* ≥ 0.976. The specific gap-in-the-new-direction geometry
  carries no forecasting information. The kicker is a vivid name for two big candles and a gap,
  not a turn predictor.
